messages.subject: Weird results with confint()
parts:
I seem to be getting weird results using the confint function for single season occupancy estimates. Here is a simpler scenario than what I am working with, but I think it still gets to my point.

I am trying to get occupancy estimates for categorial covariates and I am using something similar to 

backTransform(linearComb(fm['state'],c(1,0,0))) #Cat1 - my data is set up so that my intercept is Cat1
backTransform(linearComb(fm['state'],c(1,1,0))) #Cat2
backTransform(linearComb(fm['state'],c(1,0,1))) #Cat3

Then:
pl=confint(fm,type="state",method="profile")
pl.table=plogis(pl)

**I have also tried with the Ward confidence intervals**

This is giving me confidence intervals that do not fall around my estimates. I was a bit confused so did a some extra investigating.

Using predict(), I get the same estimates as the above backTransform set up and CI's that are legit.
With the confint code above I seem to be getting CI's that would fall around estimates and seem reasonable if I changed my linear combo to not include a "1" for the intercept
e.g. backTransform(linearComb(fm['state'],c(0,0,1))) #Cat3

Its late on a Sunday, so it could very well be something that I coded wrong, but I seem to be a bit turned around on this one.

Cheers.

Travis
